SUSE CSAF adapter fixtures
==========================

Acquired over HTTPS on 2026-10-10 from SUSE's security automation publication.
All retained JSON, checksum, signature, and key files contain the original
response bytes without trimming, reformatting, field projection, or fabricated
records. Local basenames add "suse-" to identify this adapter's ownership.

Vendor: SUSE Product Security Team, https://www.suse.com/
License: CC-BY-4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
Published license: https://ftp.suse.com/pub/projects/security/csaf/LICENSE
Each JSON document also carries SUSE's CC-BY-4.0 legal_disclaimer note and
copyright notice. Attribution and original notices are retained unchanged.

This is SUSE-SU-2024:2275-1, the CVE-2024-6387 OpenSSH security update.
The vendor initial_release_date is 2024-07-03T21:59:21Z; its later CSAF
current_release_date is not substituted for that publication date. The binary
openssh-server fixed package is 0:9.6p1-150600.6.3.1. Native RPM comparison
retains the SUSE backported revision rather than replacing it with an upstream
OpenSSH release. Tests' preceding/succeeding EVRs are comparison inputs, not
claims that SUSE published those particular builds.

Products are explicit CSAF default_component_of relationships to platform
products. The same document independently identifies SLES 15 SP6, SLES for SAP,
Desktop, modules, and openSUSE Leap 15.6. Only exact base-SLES or Leap CPEs are
selected. The Leap i586 relationship exists while base SLES i586 does not.
No binary-to-source mapping is inferred from the PURL upstream qualifier.

This genuine Tumbleweed notice describes accumulated fixes on GA media, not a
first-fixed EVR. It lists thttpd 2.29-3.9 although its CVE description says
CVE-2017-17663 affected thttpd before 2.28. The adapter refuses GA-media notices:
it must not label every older package vulnerable merely because a newer GA
package is recommended. Such refusal leaves coverage unknown. Tumbleweed's
platform CPE has no snapshot date; only an explicit rolling source scope can
select it. No release date is manufactured from the document or download time.

Fixture: suse-security-automation.asc
URL: https://ftp.suse.com/pub/projects/security/keys/security-automation.asc
Bytes: 3161
SHA256: b00811fa6b54922d852839fef56e68e6059af33bc5f77483d4305db2e904ef1e
Primary/signing key fingerprint: 6B62473BD771517D41E684DFD4439E7EC133994D
UID: SUSE Security Automation Key (only for automation data) <security@suse.de>
Encryption-only subkey fingerprint: 119CE90B0CD0B33E4BB055B841E4D7BD1E7242C1
Fingerprint inspected with gpg --batch --no-options --with-colons --show-keys.
The key is public verification material, not a credential. Its purpose and UID
remain intact. Public-key and detached-signature publication is not itself a
claim that cryptographic verification has run in these parser tests.

Authentication boundary
-----------------------
The published SHA256 values matched the acquired JSON byte digests. SUSE also
publishes the retained detached OpenPGP signatures. Online acquisition must
check the companion checksum and verify signatures against an explicitly
trusted/pinned automation key before parsing. An HTTPS-fetched key must not
silently become its own trust anchor. Shared acquisition/signature orchestration
is outside suse.go. Offline callers retain responsibility for authenticated
custody and pinning; parseSUSE does not claim to verify signatures.

Normalization and limitations
-----------------------------
Only finalized CSAF 2.0 security advisories with explicit platform relationships
and vendor_fix remediation are normalized. Native criteria not represented by
the normalized contract (version-range branches, groups, unresolved references,
unknown/affected statuses without a supported boundary) fail closed. Single
advisory documents always remain partial, never a clean-coverage assertion.
SLES release 15.6 selects cpe:/o:suse:sles:15:sp6, not sles_sap, sled, LTSS,
modules, Package Hub, or extensions. Leap 15.6 selects cpe:/o:opensuse:leap:15.6.

OVAL was considered, using the vendor description at
https://ftp.suse.com/pub/projects/security/oval/README. Those feeds include
multi-product criteria and (in patch form) records still in QA; the CSAF adapter
instead requires final publication plus explicit native-package relationships.

Tests also mutate decoded copies in memory to exercise refusal paths. Those
copies are deliberately invalid test inputs, not retained vendor documents.
No acquisition time, release timestamp, synthetic architecture mapping, or
source-package mapping is used to create authoritative records.

Tumbleweed OVAL source research (2026-10-11)
------------------------------------------
URL: https://ftp.suse.com/pub/projects/security/oval/opensuse.tumbleweed.xml.gz
Acquired compressed bytes: 10686297
SHA256: 61c2efd98f5ec427c8bc16710db06126c0bbc0c4ef240cfd2b10b6c3dd1d102c
Retained full research payload: ~/.cache/lindm-tier2-advisories-research/tumbleweed.xml.gz
The HTTPS download and hash above were exercised; this is not native matching
qualification or a claim of a detached vendor signature.

suse-tumbleweed-subset.xml is explicitly a projected XML test document, not
the complete vendor payload. Its generator and two complete definitions
(CVE-2001-1267 and CVE-2026-45992), and every transitively referenced native
test/object/state, retain original vendor XML fragments without rewriting.
Only the enclosing section assembly and selection are local. Projection SHA256:
c9c3e7e57b424f0bc16df400831fc7e5be1344da6ae899b87dd73d53a6ad2b42
SUSE OVAL license: CC-BY-4.0, https://ftp.suse.com/pub/projects/security/oval/LICENSE
License terms: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode
The selected original fragments retain SUSE's license; Apache-2.0 applies only
to lindm-authored sources, not a relicensing of this projected vendor dataset.
Vendor: SUSE Product Security Team. Attribution and research do not turn this
projection into a signed snapshot or native qualification record.

All 29328 downloaded vulnerability definitions bind the exact Tumbleweed CPE
and an openSUSE-release RPM >=0:20210101-0. Referenced package tests use native
EVR less-than predicates; some require all installed instances, not any one
old kernel. Unreferenced test/state entries contain additional unsupported
predicates and do not authorize any definition. The parser resolves references
instead of reading display comments. The generator timestamp lacks an offset;
freshness conservatively starts 14 hours earlier than the displayed wall time.
The export does not assert complete historical/third-party/unfixed coverage.
The patch export is not substituted: SUSE says it also contains patches in QA.
